dataset.name: WTC 1 V8I-A mechanically bounded core slab catenary
dataset.scope: Floors 94-99; reduced-order vertical transfer through core beams and a cracked reinforced-slab membrane
dataset.warning: The as-built core slab reinforcement schedule, Drawing Book 5 beam schedule, Drawing Book 6 connection schedule, floor openings and the NIST adjusted global-model slab modulus are unavailable. Every slab case below is a declared sensitivity envelope, not an as-built assignment.

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: The Floor 96 core used a 4.5 in concrete slab supported by wide-flange girders and beams connected to core columns with bolted connections; this passage calls the concrete lightweight.
official_facts.confidence: high; visually checked against the rendered page

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: The core floor slab was typically 4.5 in concrete, composite with floor beams through shear studs; this passage calls the concrete normal weight.
official_facts.confidence: high; extracted text checked in the official local PDF

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: NIST gives typical slab reinforcement ratios of 0.21 percent in the primary-truss direction and 0.74 percent transversely.
official_facts.confidence: high; visually checked, but the passage describes the typical tower slab and does not uniquely establish the core slab schedule at Floors 94-99

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: A smeared welded-wire-fabric representation used 0.47 percent reinforcement and 70 ksi wire yield strength in a NIST component model.
official_facts.confidence: high for the NIST model input; low for direct transfer to the as-built core slab

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: The global model used the drawing thickness for the core slab but adjusted its elastic modulus to match the in-plane stiffness of the composite steel-beam and slab system. NIST reports local redistribution among neighboring columns.
official_facts.confidence: high; the numerical adjusted modulus is not reported on the inspected page

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: The global shell floors were intended to provide diaphragm action and transfer load from a shortening core to the exterior wall, but their elevated-temperature failure modes were imposed separately as fire-induced damage.

official_facts.label: FAIT_OBSERVE_TRANSCRIT_PAR_NIST
official_facts.fact: WTC 1 was impacted at 8:46:26 and began to collapse at 10:28:20, 102 min after impact.
official_facts.confidence: high; observation table in the official report

documented_contradictions.subject: core slab concrete type
documented_contradictions.treatment: V8I does not use concrete tensile stiffness; the contradiction therefore affects omitted mass/compression behavior, not the cracked-reinforcement catenary law.

model_hypotheses.topology: nearest-four connected proxy inherited from V8H; not the as-built beam/slab mesh
model_hypotheses.core_area: convex hull of reconstructed core column centrelines; floor openings and slab beyond the column-centre hull are not explicitly meshed
model_hypotheses.strip_width: one isotropic network is area-normalized so sum(edge length times effective width) equals twice the active convex-hull area, representing two reinforcement directions without assigning a real strip to any edge
model_hypotheses.slab_mechanism: cracked reinforcement-only catenary in parallel with the V8H bilinear beam spring; concrete tensile resistance is set to zero
model_hypotheses.slab_temperature: either 20 C as an optimistic upper bound or the mean synthetic temperature of the edge endpoint columns as a proxy
model_hypotheses.beam_case: 14WF136 proxy, connection factor 1.0, two active floor planes, endpoint-mean temperature; chosen before V8I execution as the middle V8H section with optimistic connection participation
model_hypotheses.vertical_coupling: stable column reactions at one story become nodal loads at the story below

slab_cases.interpretation: V8H beam-only reference on the selected topology and beam case
lower sensitivity envelope: low documented directional ratio, reduced active area, lower assumed yield and ductility
low documented directional ratio over the full area proxy
high documented directional ratio but only one quarter of the convex-hull area active
strong documented directional ratio over the full area proxy
deliberately optimistic upper envelope: full proxy area, high ratio, cold reinforcement and high assumed ductility

ensemble.column_damage_rule: NIST Case B more-severe impact state; severed and heavy segments removed only on reported floors
ensemble.warning: Every synthetic field spans the NIST floor minimum and maximum. Fractions measure robustness to these constructed fields, not event probabilities.
